title: Anchor / originate / lifecycle-event schemas: accept and anchor platform-s's non-PII actor + organisation identity fields (actorDid, actorLevel, actorSource, actorVerified, orgDid, orgTrust, orgVerified) beside identityCommitment
description:
## What platform-s needs

Follow-on to [KS-721](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-721/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-opaque-identitycommitment) (which accepted `metadata.identityCommitment`). Platform-S now needs the Cardano record to **show** who acted and at what identity level, for the actor and their organisation — readable, not only committed. The S-side ruling on what is allowed in clear is [PS-869](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-869/5-decision-the-on-chain-identity-record-did-level-source-and-verified) (decision) under epic [PS-864](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-864/epic-id-status-stored-and-shown-throughout-the-system-actor-and); the field list there is the contract:

| Field | Type | Pattern / values |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `actorDid` | string ≤ 512 | `^did:(key|web):[A-Za-z0-9._:%-]+$` |
| `actorLevel` | integer | `1`, `2`, `3` — NIST 800-63A IAL alignment |
| `actorSource` | string | `platform` | `stripe` | `entra-verified-id` |
| `actorVerified` | boolean |  |
| `orgDid` | string ≤ 512 | as `actorDid` |
| `orgTrust` | string | `unverified` | `domain` | `document` | `kyc` | `government` |
| `orgVerified` | boolean |  |
| `identityCommitment` | string ≤ 128 | already accepted ([KS-721](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-721/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-opaque-identitycommitment)); the `vN` will move to `v2` |

All optional; all non-PII (DIDs are pseudonymous, levels and sources are enumerations, no dates, no names, no emails). Consistent with [KS-240](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-240/strict-by-default-on-chain-minimisation-strip-issuername-any-human) — no free text, nothing recoverable to a natural person.

## Suggested work

1. Accept the block as `metadata.identity` (or flat under `metadata` — say which) on **every** endpoint S anchors through: `POST /api/anchors`, `POST /api/documents` (originate), `POST /{id}/version`, `POST /{id}/anchor`, `POST /{id}/share`, `POST /{id}/transfer-custody`, `POST /api/certifications/issue`, `POST /{id}/lifecycle-events`. Today `anchorSchema.ts` strips unknown keys, so S will not send until K is live (the [PS-612](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-612/rename-the-certify-verb-to-declare-across-s) ordering).
2. Carry it into the on-chain record beside `documentType` / `occurredAt` / `identityCommitment`.
3. Return it in provenance / verify / anchor-status responses so S can render "on chain: Level 2, entra-verified-id" beside its local snapshot and flag any mismatch.
4. **State which existing request fields reach Cardano metadata**: `holderEmail`, `recipients[].email`, `newHolderEmail`, `onBehalfOf.email` / `displayName`. S sends these today; the requirement is that no PII is stored on the blockchain. If any of them is written to chain metadata, file the defect and link it here.
5. OpenAPI spec + Schemathesis / Akto examples updated in the same PR ([KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage) pattern), and both K-side testing HTML docs.

## Ordering

**K deploys first**, then PS-870 adds the fields on the S request. Pair-test from S against K on paired slots (S slot N ↔ K slot N) and quote the counts.

Each of the six weakenings planted alone is killed (the `m` flag 4 red cells, `=` 2, `$` dropped 10, the `i` flag 2, `+` to `*` 2, `\s` 8); all six at once turn 14 of 135 red, exactly the 14 new RED cells, and no older cell goes red. @kamil.kreiser — **contract amendment from S (Stuart's ruling on PS-1324, 22 Oct 2026): please widen `actorDid` / `orgDid` to accept `did:jwk` as well.**

| Field | Was | Now |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `actorDid`, `orgDid` | `^did:(key|web):[A-Za-z0-9._:%-]+$`, ≤ 512 | **`^did:(key|web|jwk):[A-Za-z0-9._:%-]+$`**, ≤ 512 |

**Why.** An actor verified through Entra Verified ID carries the credential's subject DID, which is a `did:jwk` (`did:jwk:` + base64url of the JWK; the one on dev-ps is 231 characters, alphabet `A-Za-z0-9_-`, so it already fits the character class and the length cap). S sent it verbatim; your `anchorSchema.ts:120` enforced the table above exactly, so every anchor for such an actor was refused 400 — visibly on originate, silently on certify (KS-1709). The value is as pseudonymous as a `did:key` (a public key, nothing recoverable to a person without the off-chain record), so the KS-240 / PS-869 reasoning for a DID in clear is unchanged, and S prefers one identifier per person over converting to `did:key` on the wire.

**What S does regardless (PS-1325):** a guard so S never sends a DID outside this pattern — it drops the field and logs once, ids only — shipping with the widened pattern from the start, so an S deployed before your change still sends nothing you refuse. Until the widened pattern reaches Kintsugi and demo-pk, Entra-verified actors' anchors stay refused there, and PS-870's switch stays off on uat-ps (PS-1283 is blocked on both).

**Asked of K:** the one-line `DID_PATTERN` change plus the OpenAPI spec, Schemathesis / Akto examples and the two K testing HTML docs (the KS-256 pattern), then a deploy to Kintsugi and demo-pk with a note on KS-772. If you would rather this were its own KS ticket in work-stream A or H, say so and I will not file it from here — it is your work-stream to file into.

## Finding: KS-721's commitment could never reach a real chain (KS-1284, filed 2026-09-20, `Refs KS-721`)
Cardano metadata caps every string at **64 bytes** and has **no boolean type**; CSL 15.0.3 throws at tx build (`Max metadata string too long: 69, max = 64`; `bools not allowed in metadata`). `identityCommitment` (≥69 bytes) therefore failed at `cardano/transaction.ts` on every non-mock anchor — proven in mock mode only, never hit because S has never sent it. The PR adds a codec at the two chain boundaries only: strings >64 bytes are anchored as arrays of ≤64-byte chunks (the Cardano convention), the two verified flags as `"true"`/`"false"`; K's readers undo both; the DB row and both read-backs keep the logical typed form. For every payload anchored to date the codec is a byte-identical no-op (pinned by test). An independent chain reader (Cardanoscan / raw Blockfrost) sees the array / string forms.

## Wire shape as platform-s will send it (PS-870, built 2026-09-16 behind `CardanoAnchor:AnchorIdentity`, default off)

On **every** anchored write — `POST /api/documents`, `/{id}/version`, `/{id}/share`, `/{id}/transfer-custody`, `/api/certifications/issue`, `/{id}/lifecycle-events`, `POST /api/anchors` — a **top-level** `identity` object:

```json
"identity": {
  "actorDid": "did:key:z6Mk…",         "actorLevel": 2,          "actorSource": "stripe",
  "actorVerified": true,
  "orgDid": "did:web:acme.example",     "orgTrust": "domain",     "orgVerified": true,
  "identityCommitment": "identity-commitment-l2.v1:<64 hex>"
}
```

- Absent fields are omitted (never `null` / `""`); a row with no snapshot sends no `identity` key at all.
- `actorLevel` ∈ {1,2,3}; `actorSource` ∈ {`platform`,`stripe`,`entra-verified-id`}; `orgTrust` ∈ {`unverified`,`domain`,`document`,`kyc`,`government`}.
- On `POST /api/anchors` the commitment ALSO rides as `metadata.identityCommitment` (the KS-721 field). Note the purpose is now `identity-commitment-l2` (layout 2 covers the organisation) — still matches KS-721's pattern `^[a-z0-9-]+\.v\d+:[0-9a-f]{64}$`.
- Read-back: S records whatever the anchor GET returns under `identityCommitment` and `identity` into `DocumentTransaction.AnchorIdentityJson` on confirmation, so returning them on `GET /api/anchors/{id}` is what makes the local-vs-chain comparison possible (PS-871).

S will not turn the switch on for an environment until its K confirms this contract — a K that strips the key makes anchors look identity-evidenced while carrying nothing.
